title: Five of the six sc_stale rows cite no source past its freshness lifetime, so they no longer measure staleness
goal: Each sc_stale row of bench_pool.csv asks a question whose pack cites a source past its freshness lifetime, so pool check prints no 'cites no source past its freshness lifetime' warning; rows rebuilt through bench_scenarios.csv, no paid run without its dry-run estimate

run: import sys,subprocess;o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/benchmarks.py','pool','check'],capture_output=True,text=True);n=(o.stdout+o.stderr).count('cites no source past');print(n,o.returncode);sys.exit(1 if n or o.returncode else 0)

clauses.clause: Each sc_stale row of bench_pool.csv asks a question whose pack cites a source past its freshness lifetime, so pool check prints no 'cites no source past its freshness lifetime' warning

notes: Premise: pool check prints the warning for four rows today (BP-b9e93043, BP-9cf2c396, BP-fa7d95f6, BP-4edc88f0; BP-7579b23f and BP-2c2a3c1d still cite a stale source: S-sdxhnx3i, S-lz7th2mw and S-3yod3u7q); the repro exits 1 with 4. Plan: replace each of the four questions in bench_scenarios.csv by one whose pack cites a source kbfacts.source_freshness reads as stale, and update only those pool rows (scenario_built), not a whole-pool rebuild. No paid call is needed (eval checks are cached): a pool build --dry-run into a scratch copy prints no 'would ask'; read its output before any build. Rows of BG-3yjnwfsu (BP-2c2a3c1d) land first. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 5 of 15, "Benchmark pool rows: answer regexes, stale rows, the gap row, a pool build that asks before paying and a corrected report"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed.
